_doc: Agent invocation profiles — the Parameter Object for every LLM call in the pipeline.
WHY THIS EXISTS. Before this file, all 15 invocation sites hand-assembled their own
env bundle, and every site omitted a different subset: no shell site set a timeout,
13 of 15 never set ORCH_JSON_RESULT (so per-agent cost was invisible), and 5 set no
output budget at all — which on 2026-07-25 made the team-lead reviewer emit 169 bytes
of truncated <think> instead of a verdict and blocked a metrolinx run. Each omission
was found by a LIVE RUN, one at a time, because 'a call site forgot a parameter' is
invisible to a test that checks behaviour one site at a time.
THE FIX IS STRUCTURAL, NOT A DEFAULT. Call sites no longer pass execution parameters;
they name a ROLE. lib/agent-invoke.sh resolves the role here, validates that every
required key is present (fail-fast — an incomplete profile aborts the run loudly
rather than silently running at 4096), and exports the whole set. You cannot forget a
parameter you never supply.
SPLIT OF CONCERNS. Routing (which model/provider, ladder escalation, retry tiers) stays
with the caller — it is genuinely per-site and dynamic. The EXECUTION BUDGET lives here.
That is precisely the parameter set that kept getting dropped.
anything under ~8192 risks the model spending its whole allowance thinking and
returning a truncated fragment. Do not lower these below 8192 for a reasoning model.
SIZING IS EVIDENCE-BASED (2026-07-25). Two independent sources agreed:
MEASURED, 794 real calls from this pipeline via Langfuse: reasoning is the budget,
not the answer. One glm-5.1 call counted 7,230 output tokens while returning 332
CHARACTERS of visible text (~85 tokens). In aggregate 64% of glm-5.1's and 37% of
glm-5.2's output tokens are invisible thinking. Truncations by budget, out of 794:
at exactly 16384, and glm-5.1 produced a LEGITIMATE 16,403-token completion.
VENDOR-VERIFIED (live probes + docs): reasoning tokens are deducted from max_tokens
on glm-5.1, glm-5.2, kimi-k3 and minimax-m3 — probed with max_tokens:200, all four
spent the ENTIRE budget thinking and returned EMPTY content with HTTP 200. Moonshot
documents 'set max_tokens >= 16000 ... without truncation'; OpenAI advises reserving
>= 25,000; Anthropic 16,000+ for complex work. Artificial Analysis measures GLM-5.2
at ~43k output per task, 37k of it reasoning.
So 32768: above every call we have ever observed, above every vendor floor, and
safely under the LOWEST per-provider ceiling on OpenRouter (65,535 — glm-5.1 ranges
65,535-202,752 across providers and OpenRouter load-balances between them).
Raising a cap costs NOTHING: max_tokens is a ceiling, not a reservation, and billing
is on tokens generated. Median real output is 108 tokens. Capping low does not make
the model think less — it cuts it off mid-thought, and you pay for the wasted tokens
AND the escalation retry. That is the 169-byte reviewer.
reasoning.max_tokens is NOT supported on these models (probed: glm-5.1 ignores it).
The only working lever is full off: reasoning:{enabled:false} (5.1) /
reasoning:{effort:'none'} (5.2), both verified. Worth using for structured-JSON
gates that do not need deep reasoning — safer and cheaper than budget-tuning.
agentSeams and seamPatterns map a MINTED AGENT to its ARCHETYPE — the base agent it is an instance of.

It is not a bag of invocation settings that happen to suit. The distinction matters because an archetype carries what an instance INHERITS; an implementer pointed at a diagnostician would inherit the wrong prompt, the wrong output kind and the wrong inputs.

team-lead-review._what: Reviews the story's code change AND its test; emits a verdict.

agent-failure-analyst._what: Diagnoses a no-output/failed agent attempt, prescribes a corrective directive.

repro-test-writer._what: Writes the bug-reproducing test for a brownfield fix.

consumes._note: NOT required, for the same reason as story-writer: DET-1 made "investigated, found nothing" a legitimate state. A reproducing test is written from the failure, and requiring a plan would refuse the story on any codeline where the detective found nothing — a hard failure for a state the pipeline treats as normal.

tc-writer._what: Writes post-implementation test criteria into the PRD.

cpa-gate._what: Judges a CPA estimate rewrite: pass/fail.

cpa-inference._what: Produces the cost/effort estimate for a story.

prd-change-reviewer._what: Reviews a proposed PRD mutation before it is applied.

prd-change-summarizer._what: Summarizes a rewrite for the change log.

impl-failure-analyst._what: Diagnoses why an implementation attempt failed.

ac-elaboration._what: Elaborates an acceptance criterion into verification criteria.

codeline-discovery._what: Picks which local codeline a Jira ticket belongs to.

roster-review._what: Falsifies the claims in a generated agent roster before any implementer inherits them.

code-graph-detective._what: Investigates one codeline and reports where the work actually lands.

guard-vocabulary._what: Derives the vocabulary the verification-criteria guard enforces. A guard armed with the wrong terms reports clean.

estate-survey._what: Surveys every codeline BEFORE the roster is minted: which ones the work actually reaches, and which need their own investigator. Breadth, never fix sites.

story-writer._what: Implements a story: writes the code that satisfies its criteria. The archetype every minted -engineer is an instance of.
story-writer._note: The writer is invoked today through claude.sh own rung ladder, not through this seam, so these settings are not yet the live invocation path. The record exists because an instance must inherit from the archetype it IS: -engineer resolved to impl-failure-analyst purely because that ladder matched the tier wanted, which makes an implementer an instance of a diagnostician.

consumes._note: NOT required: DET-1 made "investigated, found nothing" a legitimate state, and claude.sh has carried that reasoning since 2026-08-08. Requiring a plan would refuse to build prompts the pipeline is supposed to build. The authority under which the writer reads a plan that IS present lives in the story-writer prompt document, body "fix-plan" — prompt text belongs in a prompt file.

consumes.authority: must be addressed before this is accepted

vc-coverage._what: Judges whether the written tests cover each verification criterion.

qa-gate:sast._what: Static application security scan over the change.

qa-gate:spec-validator._what: Checks the change satisfies the story’s acceptance criteria.

qa-gate:review-ranger._what: Reviews the change for defects the team-lead review may not reach.

qa-gate:mutant-hunter._what: Assesses whether the tests would fail if the change were broken.

qa-gate:fuzz-weaver._what: Probes the change with adversarial inputs.

qa-gate:perf-sentinel._what: Assesses the change for runtime and startup cost.

_seamResolution: HOW ANY AGENT — INCLUDING ONE MINTED THIS RUN — FINDS ITS SEAM.
A run mints agents whose names cannot exist in this file: gotransit-investigator,
profiles, and every unnamed one resolved to {} — no ladder, no effort, no temperature, and
nothing said so. Resolution is now TOTAL and is tried in this order:
1. profiles[<agent>]     the agent IS a seam
2. agentSeams[<agent>]   explicit cross-reference: this agent enters by this seam
3. seamPatterns          a name SHAPE maps to a seam, so agents not yet invented resolve
5. THROW                 never {}. An unresolvable agent fails at mint time, where it can
be fixed, not three hours into a run running unconfigured.
The engine holds none of these names. Adding an agent kind is an edit HERE.

seamPatterns._why: investigates one codeline and reports where the work lands
same investigation seam under its other minted suffix
validates a proposed artefact before it is applied
checks an artefact against a standard
detects a defect class in an artefact
plans and estimates rather than producing code
implements the story — the archetype it is an instance of, not merely a profile whose ladder matches
generic minted worker; medium ladder until given a specific seam

_publishesVia: An archetype carrying publishesVia="agent-io" has been migrated onto the published-inputs framework: it renders its own output and publishes it. Required-input enforcement applies ONLY to kinds whose producer carries this marker — a kind still rendered the old way has nothing in the store, and refusing every prompt over that would stop the pipeline rather than migrate it. Each producer gains the marker as it moves; when every producer has one, the marker and this note go.
_ladderPositions: A seam declares a POSITION in the project’s ladderTierOrder (base|mid|top), never a tier NAME. The project owns its tier vocabulary; the engine owns none. Converted 2026-08-15 after twenty seams asking for a literal HIGHEST ran unladdered on a project that declared only high and medium.
